prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the continuous ground plane of the open parking lot across all five frames, showing the asphalt receding smoothly from about 1–2 m at the bottom edge to over 30 m in the background, with the storefront wall on the left in frames 1 and 4 at roughly 3–15 m. In frame 1, a bright silhouette in the lower-left foreground marks an upright curbside object (about 1.5–2 m away, just outside arm's reach), while frame 2 is dominated by a bright near-field gradient (1–4 m) as the camera pitches down toward the pavement. Across frames 3 to 5, as the camera turns right, left, and right again, the dark SUV stands out as a mid-grey silhouette that shifts from the center-right at roughly 5–7 m (frame 3), to the right edge at 4–5 m where it is half cropped out of view (frame 4), and to the left at 6–8 m (frame 5), while a partially visible person on the far right edge of frame 3 appears brighter at about 2–3 m in front of the SUV. The map clearly separates the foreground person and mid-ground SUV from the background cars 10–40 m behind them—distances that flatten in the wide-angle RGB—and shows nothing within immediate arm's reach (<1 m) of the camera wearer. However, the depth map is unreliable at far ranges (>20 m) where parked cars, light poles, and sky merge into uniform black, and it provides no facial or gaze detail to tell which way people are looking.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete vehicles and pedestrians against a black background across the parking lot, detecting distant cars at 20–40 m in frame 1, nothing in the downward-tilted frame 2, and rows of parked cars spanning 10–50 m left to right in frames 3 through 5. In frame 3, a large cyan mask outlines the left-facing dark SUV at roughly 5–7 m in the center-right, occluding the front of the parked car row behind it, while smaller masks to its right identify a close person at 2–3 m on the far-right frame boundary (mostly out of view, oriented left) and a distant person and car about 20–25 m away (~15–20 m behind the SUV). As the camera wearer turns left in frame 4 and back right in frame 5, the cyan SUV mask shifts to the right edge at 4–5 m (partially out of view) and then to the left at 6–8 m, moving relative to the background car masks spaced 2–4 m apart from each other. This map makes it easier than RGB alone to count individual overlapping parked cars in the distant rows and to spot the small distant pedestrian next to the SUV in frame 3. However, it is unreliable in several places: it completely misses the foreground curbside object in frame 1, all parked cars in frame 2, and the building and ground plane throughout, while falsely labeling a high lamppost at the top-left of frame 3 (above the cars, ~25 m away) as a 'kite' and failing to indicate anyone's gaze direction or arm's-reach proximity.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, providing no body or hand skeleton detections anywhere in the parking lot scene. Using the RGB strip for context, the scene actually contains a person standing about 2–3 m to the right in frame 3 (heavily occluded by the right frame edge, facing roughly left with their head cropped out) and at least two smaller pedestrians about 20–25 m away in the right background behind the dark SUV, none of whom are within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of the nearby SUV (~3–4 m separates the foreground person from the SUV). Across the five frames, as the camera pitches down toward the ground in frame 2 and pans between the left storefront (3–15 m) and the mid-ground SUV (4–8 m) in frames 3–5, no people enter the central field of view or come within arm's reach (<1 m) of the camera wearer. Because the map contains zero skeletons, it adds no spatial information beyond confirming the absence of close, fully visible people in the center of the walkway, and it cannot show head orientation, gaze direction toward the camera wearer, or hand positions. The map is unreliable for the cropped person at the right boundary of frame 3 and for the distant pedestrians 20–25 m away, where severe edge truncation and small pixel scale cause complete detection failure.
